pillars.name: Anyonic computation
pillars.statement: Quantum information can be stored in the fusion space of non-Abelian anyons and processed by braiding and fusion.
pillars.dbeGoal: Give the topological core an instruction set that is physically fault-tolerant.
pillars.engineNote: Maps to E-S3. Load-bearing topological primitive.

pillars.name: Majorana braid core
pillars.statement: Ising / Majorana zero modes realise the simplest non-Abelian braid group that hardware can host.
pillars.dbeGoal: A register whose gates are worldline topology, not pulse amplitude.
pillars.engineNote: Do not make load-bearing. Parallel watch item.

pillars.name: Fracton memory
pillars.statement: Restricted-mobility excitations confine errors, enabling long-lived quantum memory without constant active correction.
pillars.dbeGoal: Hold plasma-state snapshots long enough for predictive control.
pillars.engineNote: Theory workstream. CUT from hardware stack.

pillars.name: Floquet time-crystal clock
pillars.statement: A discrete time crystal supplies a subharmonic tick that is robust to drive noise.
pillars.dbeGoal: Synchronise braids, memory scrubs, and actuator fires on one clock.
pillars.engineNote: Many-body physics study. CUT as metronome.

pillars.name: Holographic encoding
pillars.statement: Bulk reconstruction is a quantum error-correcting code: a lower-dimensional boundary can protect a high-dimensional interior.
pillars.dbeGoal: Compress tokamak profiles into a boundary representation the controller can store and invert.
pillars.engineNote: Reading list only. Not a reactor or processor subsystem.

pillars.name: Learned plasma control
pillars.statement: Deep RL can command magnetic coils at experimental rates and shape previously inaccessible plasmas.
pillars.dbeGoal: Close the loop from topological prediction to RMP coils and pellets.

pillars.name: Modular fusion–quantum stack
pillars.statement: A modular processor that couples topological compute to a reactor, with DBE-S demanding honest Q accounting toward Q = 1000.
pillars.dbeGoal: The program-level target: Q = 1000 with physically valid loss channels.
pillars.engineNote: Q=1000 is a ledger stress test, not an output.

pillars.name: Cyclic fusion universality
pillars.statement: Minimally non-Abelian orders (S3) are not braid-universal, but become universal when fusion measurement is a primitive.
pillars.dbeGoal: Use the simplest scalable non-Abelian order that still compiles a complete gate set.
pillars.whySuggested: Nature 2026 shows S3 on 54 qubits is preparable and computationally complete once fusion is allowed. That is a new pillar, not just a data point.
pillars.engineNote: Promoted in place: S3 braid+fusion is the 2026 hardware path. Status was 'suggested'; engine freeze treats it as KEEP under E-S3.

pillars.name: Floquet–Majorana codes
pillars.statement: Measurement schedules can switch the same logical qubit between static and dynamical representatives.
pillars.dbeGoal: One hardware family for both the clock and the braid register.
pillars.whySuggested: Unifies two DBE subsystems that the white paper treats as separate boxes.
pillars.engineNote: Would couple E-MZM and E-TC. Coupling starts at C1.

pillars.name: Fracton topological holography
pillars.statement: SymTFT / topological holography extends from liquid topological order to fracton stabilizer codes.
pillars.dbeGoal: Give fracton memory a holographic compression language instead of ad-hoc block averaging.
pillars.whySuggested: Connects two existing pillars with a shared bulk-boundary language.

pillars.name: Non-Abelian qLDPC / 2D universality
pillars.statement: Non-Abelian stabilizer and qLDPC constructions may finish a universal gate set in strictly two dimensions.
pillars.dbeGoal: Keep the topological core planar, matching tokamak diagnostics and 2D anyon braiding.
pillars.whySuggested: Removes a hidden 3D overhead that would break DBE’s modular, planar control story.
pillars.engineNote: Interesting Bus B research; not a new engine pillar until an interface contract exists.

pillars.name: Topological hardware for dynamics
pillars.statement: Fibonacci / Ising braids can compile molecular and condensed-phase propagators, including nonlinear fluids.
pillars.dbeGoal: Put plasma transport on the same processor that braids anyons.
pillars.whySuggested: This is the first credible path from ‘quantum subsystem stub’ to actual dynamics simulation inside the engine.
pillars.engineNote: Bus B simulation path. Fail if slower than classical HPC.

pillars.name: Spacetime fractons / Floquet-immobile excitations
pillars.statement: Floquet codes can host excitations immobile in both space and time, unifying memory and clock as one object.
pillars.dbeGoal: Only if an interface contract exists. Currently a monthly NEW PILLAR candidate.
pillars.engineNote: Queued 2026-09-20. Needs in/out/latency/fail-safe. Opportunity cost: attention on E-S3 / E-RL / S-L2.
pillars.whySuggested: Prettiest unification of two HOLD items. Protocol still forbids load-bearing.

pillars.name: Spacetime-fracton Floquet codes
pillars.statement: Fractalizing spacetime yields Floquet codes whose excitations are immobile in space and time.
pillars.dbeGoal: One dynamical object instead of a separate memory and clock — only if it attaches to Bus B without 3D hardware.
pillars.whySuggested: Unifies two HOLD/CUT boxes. Queued; Auto-Gate forbids opening it automatically.

pillars.name: Cyclic fusion families (Haagerup–Izumi)
pillars.statement: Cyclic fusion categories a×a=a+… exist at every odd order, so braid+fusion universality is a family, not a one-off S3 trick.
pillars.dbeGoal: A broader compiler target than S3, still with integer quantum dimension.
pillars.engineNote: Needs an interface contract. S3 remains the load-bearing primitive (E-S3). Do not displace KEEP.
pillars.whySuggested: 2609.15986 constructs cyclic Haagerup–Izumi fusion at every odd n≥3.

papers.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons
papers.coreIdea: If you make exotic quasiparticles in a 2D lattice, moving them around each other performs quantum gates, and fusing them reads the answer. Local noise cannot easily see the information because it lives in how the particles are tangled, not in any one spin.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the operating system of the DBE topological core: braiding as computation, fusion as readout, energy gap as error suppression.
papers.limitation: The original toric-code anyons are Abelian and not computationally universal; you need richer anyons (or extra fusion tricks) for a complete gate set.

papers.title: Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation
papers.coreIdea: A field-defining review: what non-Abelian statistics actually means, why Fibonacci anyons are universal from braiding alone, and why Ising / ν = 5/2 anyons are not — unless you add extra resources.
papers.whyItMatters: It is the map of which anyon theories can run a universal DBE core, and which ones need fusion measurements or magic states.
papers.limitation: Much of the hardware discussion is quantum-Hall era; trapped-ion and superconducting lattice realisations came later.

papers.title: Anyons in an exactly solved model and beyond
papers.coreIdea: A honeycomb spin model that can be solved exactly and hosts Majorana fermions plus a vortex anyon. Depending on the couplings you get either a gapped non-Abelian phase or an Abelian one.
papers.whyItMatters: It is the cleanest lattice origin story for the Majorana braid register the white paper assumes.
papers.limitation: Material realisations (α-RuCl3 and cousins) remain debated; the model is exact, the laboratory is not.

papers.title: Unpaired Majorana fermions in quantum wires
papers.coreIdea: A 1D p-wave superconducting wire can host unpaired Majorana zero modes at its ends. Braiding those modes implements a protected, if incomplete, gate set — the simplest hardware picture of a topological qubit.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the origin of the DBE Majorana braid register: not a metaphor, a lattice Hamiltonian whose end modes are the qubits.
papers.limitation: Ising / Majorana braids are not universal by themselves. Andreev bound states and disorder can mimic the zero-bias signature without topological protection.

papers.title: The large N limit of superconformal field theories and supergravity
papers.coreIdea: A quantum field theory on a boundary can be dual to gravity in a higher-dimensional bulk. Information about the interior is encoded, redundantly, on the surface.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the physical metaphor for DBE holographic compression: store a high-dimensional plasma interior as a lower-dimensional boundary code.
papers.limitation: AdS/CFT is a duality for specific supersymmetric theories, not a drop-in compressor for tokamak MHD. The engine uses the error-correction reading, not the string-theory one.

papers.title: Quantum time crystals
papers.coreIdea: Wilczek asked whether a quantum system can spontaneously tick — breaking time-translation symmetry the way a crystal breaks space-translation symmetry.
papers.whyItMatters: It names the clock the DBE wants: a time crystal as a synchronisation layer, not a metaphor.
papers.limitation: The original equilibrium proposal does not work; Watanabe and Oshikawa showed no-go theorems for ground-state time crystals. The surviving version is Floquet (driven).

papers.title: Absence of quantum time crystals
papers.coreIdea: A no-go: a quantum system in equilibrium cannot oscillate forever in its ground state. Time crystals, if they exist, need drive, dissipation, or other loopholes.
papers.whyItMatters: It forces the DBE clock onto the Floquet path — periodic drive, not a magical idle oscillator. That is why the white paper specifies a Floquet time crystal.
papers.limitation: No-gos constrain equilibrium; they do not forbid discrete time crystals in driven, many-body-localised, or open systems.

papers.title: Floquet time crystals
papers.coreIdea: Under a periodic drive, a many-body system can respond at a multiple of the drive period — a discrete time crystal — protected by many-body localisation.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the actual clock: a subharmonic tick the DBE can lock actuators and braid steps to.
papers.limitation: Requires a drive and (in the original argument) localisation or prethermal protection. It is not a free lunch thermally.

papers.title: Analytic and numerical demonstration of quantum self-correction in the 3D Cubic Code
papers.coreIdea: Haah’s 3D cubic code stores quantum information so that local errors cannot freely hop. Memory time grows with system size below a critical temperature — a genuine self-correcting quantum memory.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the existence proof for fracton memory, the DBE’s proposed long-term store for plasma snapshots.
papers.limitation: It is a 3D lattice model with no-go tension against 2D self-correction. Engineering a physical fracton memory remains open.

papers.title: Fracton phases of matter
papers.venue: International Journal of Modern Physics A
papers.coreIdea: A review of quasiparticles that cannot move by themselves (fractons), or only along lines or planes. Restricted mobility is a conservation law, not a bug, and it links spin liquids, elasticity, gravity analogies, and quantum memory.
papers.whyItMatters: It is the field guide for why fracton order is the right language for an error-confining DBE memory.
papers.limitation: Most models are exactly solvable lattice Hamiltonians; experimental fracton matter is still largely prospective.

papers.title: Bulk locality and quantum error correction in AdS/CFT
papers.coreIdea: The holographic dictionary is a quantum error-correcting code: bulk operators are reconstructable from different boundary patches the way logical qubits are reconstructable from different subsets of physical qubits.
papers.whyItMatters: It turns holography from poetry into an encoder specification for the DBE compression block.
papers.limitation: The code properties are proven in toy models (and argued in AdS/CFT), not in a plasma-state tensor network with real diagnostic noise.

papers.title: Universal gates via fusion and measurement operations on SU(2)₄ anyons
papers.coreIdea: Some anyon theories cannot compute everything by braiding alone. If you also allow fusion measurements, SU(2)₄ (and related cyclic theories) become universal.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the theorem behind the 2026 S₃ experiment: fusion is not just readout, it is a gate primitive. DBE should treat measurement as part of the compiler.
papers.limitation: The construction is algebraic. Leakage, adaptive depth, and hardware-level fusion still have to be engineered.

papers.title: Error correction for non-Abelian topological quantum computation
papers.coreIdea: Non-Abelian anyons are not automatically error-free. You still need an active decoder, because stray anyons and thermal pairs will pollute the fusion space.
papers.whyItMatters: Kills a common overclaim in TQC: topology reduces error rates, it does not delete the need for correction. The DBE braid core must budget a decoder.
papers.limitation: Thresholds are model-dependent; later work (Lyons–Brown 2026) pushes the full fault-tolerance theorem further.

papers.title: Magnetic control of tokamak plasmas through deep reinforcement learning
papers.coreIdea: A deep RL agent learned to command TCV’s magnetic coils in real time, producing standard shapes plus exotic ones (negative triangularity, snowflake, even two plasmas at once).
papers.whyItMatters: This is the existence proof that a learned controller can sit on a real tokamak at experimental rates — the actuator half of the DBE loop.
papers.limitation: It shapes plasma, it does not yet predict disruptions with a topological processor, and it does not touch Q = 1000 thermodynamics.

papers.title: Non-Abelian braiding of graph vertices in a superconducting processor
papers.coreIdea: On a superconducting chip, researchers created and braided projective non-Abelian anyons (defects of a stabilizer code) and watched the fusion outcome change because of the braid — the first on-processor observation of non-Abelian exchange.
papers.whyItMatters: It showed that ‘braid an anyon’ is no longer only a thought experiment. The DBE core can cite a hardware precedent.
papers.limitation: These are code-level anyons on a noisy processor, not thermally protected quasiparticles of a topological phase. Error correction during the braid was not complete.

papers.title: Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays
papers.coreIdea: A neutral-atom processor ran encoded logical circuits, transporting atoms to reconfigure connectivity — a hardware style that maps unusually well onto braiding worldlines.
papers.whyItMatters: Reconfigurable connectivity is what a braid compiler wants: move the support, don’t just pulse neighbours.
papers.limitation: Logical error rates still improve with more encoding, but this is not yet a topological anyon computer.

papers.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
papers.coreIdea: A superconducting surface-code experiment crossed the threshold: making the code bigger made the logical error smaller, the defining industrial test of QEC.
papers.whyItMatters: It is the Abelian baseline the DBE must beat or complement. Surface-code discipline is also how solvable quantum doubles get their decoding theorems.
papers.limitation: Surface code is not universal by braiding; it still needs magic states. Non-Abelian orders are the DBE’s proposed shortcut, not a replacement for threshold physics.

papers.title: Realization of real-time fault-tolerant quantum error correction
papers.coreIdea: Quantinuum’s trapped-ion hardware repeatedly detected and corrected errors in real time — the same stack later used to prepare S₃ topological order.
papers.whyItMatters: It is the machine lineage of the 2026 anyon-universality experiment. Real-time correction is a prerequisite for adaptive anyon circuits.
papers.limitation: The encoded distance is still modest; ‘real-time’ is not yet ‘below-threshold logical algorithms at scale’.

papers.title: Measurement as a shortcut to long-range entangled quantum matter
papers.coreIdea: Measurements plus feedback can prepare long-range entangled states (including topological order) with far shallower circuits than unitary evolution alone.
papers.whyItMatters: This is why S₃ and D₄ orders are now experimentally realistic: adaptive constant-depth recipes, not exponential cooling.
papers.limitation: Adaptive circuits need fast, high-fidelity mid-circuit measurement. Not every platform has that.

papers.title: Adaptive constant-depth circuits for manipulating non-Abelian anyons
papers.coreIdea: For quantum doubles of solvable groups, you can prepare the ground state, create distant anyon pairs, and measure topological charge with constant-depth adaptive circuits.
papers.whyItMatters: Solvable groups include S₃. This paper is why the 2026 Quantinuum experiment is called scalable rather than a one-off state-prep stunt.
papers.limitation: Constant depth is in the adaptive model. Without fast feed-forward the circuits become linear depth, which is what the experiment actually ran at 54 qubits.

papers.title: Shortest route to non-Abelian topological order on a quantum processor
papers.coreIdea: A finite-depth circuit plus one measurement layer can prepare a family of non-Abelian states (those with a Lagrangian subgroup), including D₄, without feed-forward.
papers.whyItMatters: It lowered the hardware bar for non-Abelian order and directly informed the later S₃ / D₄ experiments.
papers.limitation: D₄ is non-Abelian but not cyclic in the sense needed for fusion-universality; S₃ is the computationally richer sibling.

papers.title: Traversable wormhole dynamics on a quantum processor
papers.coreIdea: A tiny SYK-inspired circuit on Sycamore was interpreted as a traversable-wormhole teleportation protocol — holographic dynamics shrunk onto a handful of qubits.
papers.whyItMatters: It is a proof-of-attitude: holographic encoding is something you can put on hardware, not only on a blackboard. The DBE encoder should stay this honest about scale.
papers.limitation: The system is extremely small; whether it is ‘gravity’ or a clever teleportation circuit is still argued. Do not overclaim.

papers.title: Dimensional Braid Engine: a modular quantum-topological processor
papers.coreIdea: Five subsystems — Majorana braids, fracton memory, Floquet clock, holographic encoder, plasma actuators — should be one processor whose computational benchmark is extreme robustness and whose physical target is live fusion control.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the integration contract of DBE V0 / V1. Every other paper in the observatory is scored against these boxes and the Q = 1000 north star.
papers.limitation: Visionary, not a demonstrated machine. Quantum modules in the current simulator are stubs. Treat as a requirements document, not a result.

papers.title: Theoretical framework and simulation architecture for Dynamic Barrier Evasion (DBE-S) quantum fusion
papers.coreIdea: Instead of brute-force thermonuclear heating, DBE-S proposes coherent driving so nuclei tunnel a time-periodic Coulomb barrier (Floquet / multiphoton). The revision tears down naive WKB notebooks and demands open-system density matrices, unitarity-bounded cross sections, spectral hole burning, and honest Bremsstrahlung accounting on the way to Q = 1000.
papers.whyItMatters: It is the physics conscience of the fusion half: Q = 1000 is not allowed to ignore radiation, decoherence, or laser drive power.
papers.limitation: Laser-assisted nuclear tunneling at reactor scale is not experimentally established. Several layers remain theoretically ambitious; cavity-QED suppression of high-Z radiation is a proposed fix, not a measured one.

papers.title: Spin-liquid-based topological qubits
papers.coreIdea: A hardware sketch for nucleating, braiding, and reading Ising anyons in a spin liquid using magnetic tunnel junctions, with a four-anyon qubit as the minimal encoding.
papers.whyItMatters: It is a materials-side path to the Majorana/Ising register that does not assume a nanowire.
papers.limitation: Proposal-level. Creating a true non-Abelian spin liquid in a device, then braiding it, is still a stack of unproven steps.

papers.title: Projective measurements: topological quantum computing with an arbitrary number of qubits
papers.coreIdea: Braiding alone does not give you the Clifford group once you scale past two qubits. Switching encodings with projective measurements restores computational power. Simulations reach Bell and GHZ states and >99% fidelity on five-qubit random circuits.
papers.whyItMatters: Same moral as fusion-universality: measurement is part of the gate set. A DBE compiler that only braids will stall at two logical qubits.
papers.limitation: Many-body simulations, not a device. Scaling arguments still assume high-quality mid-circuit measurement.

papers.title: Universal gates from braiding and fusing anyons on quantum hardware
papers.coreIdea: On Quantinuum’s 54-qubit H2, the team prepared S₃ quantum-double topological order, encoded a qutrit in a pair of C₂ fluxes, and used braiding plus fusion measurements as a universal gate set — including a topologically prepared magic state. They also trapped a single non-Abelian anyon on a torus, a signature of cyclic fusion rules.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the flagship 2026 result for the DBE topological core: the smallest non-Abelian group is rich enough for universality and simple enough to prepare. Fusion is now an experimental primitive, not a footnote.
papers.limitation: Linear-depth circuits with post-selection at this size; constant-depth adaptive recipes exist in theory. Absolute flux encoding has a local ‘origin’ vulnerability; a relative bureau-of-standards encoding is the fully topological fix.

papers.title: Quantum computing with anyons is fault tolerant
papers.coreIdea: A full error-correction scheme for braiding anyons, with a threshold: if local noise is below a constant, the failure rate of a universal anyonic computation can be made arbitrarily small. Worked out in detail for D(S₃).
papers.whyItMatters: Kitaev argued topology is robust. This paper tries to turn that slogan into a threshold theorem for the universal (braid + fusion) gate set the 2026 experiment uses.
papers.limitation: Preprint. Threshold constants and decoder overhead will decide whether this is practical on near-term hardware.

papers.title: Non-Abelian qLDPC: TQFT formalism, addressable gauging measurement and application to magic state fountain on 2D product codes
papers.coreIdea: Extends Kitaev’s non-Abelian topological codes to qLDPC / combinatorial TQFT settings, aiming at native non-Clifford resources without jumping to 3D product codes.
papers.whyItMatters: If you can finish universality in 2D, the DBE core stays planar and compatible with anyon braiding and tokamak-side 2D control maps.
papers.limitation: Dense theory preprint. Hardware mapping and decoder cost are not yet experimental.

papers.title: High-threshold decoding of non-Pauli codes for 2D universality
authors: Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
papers.coreIdea: A non-Pauli stabilizer code that completes a universal gate set for toric/surface codes in strictly two dimensions, with a just-in-time decoder that handles mid-circuit X corrections.
papers.whyItMatters: Another 2D-universality route. Complements S₃ fusion: you might mix Abelian surface-code memory with a non-Pauli universality patch.
papers.limitation: Requires mid-circuit corrections; decoder latency vs plasma-control deadlines is unanalysed.

papers.title: Fracton topological holography
papers.coreIdea: Topological holography (SymTFT) is extended from liquid topological order to fracton stabilizer codes: symmetries and dualities of the memory become boundary data of a higher-dimensional bulk.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the missing dictionary between two DBE boxes that currently do not talk: fracton memory and holographic compression.
papers.limitation: Formal bulk-boundary construction. Not yet an encoder you can drop onto a plasma profile.

papers.title: Translation-invariant quantum LDPC codes from compactified fracton models
papers.coreIdea: Compactifying fracton models yields translation-invariant qLDPC codes — a way to harvest fracton error confinement in a more conventional code family.
papers.whyItMatters: A possible compilation path: keep fracton physics as the design principle, ship qLDPC as the engineering object.
papers.limitation: Code parameters vs Haah-type memory time are not yet a head-to-head experimental comparison.

papers.title: Subsystem symmetries and fracton models in quantum error correction
papers.coreIdea: Subsystem symmetries — symmetries that act only on lines or planes — are the right language for both fracton order and a class of QEC codes.
papers.whyItMatters: Gives the DBE memory a symmetry-based interface contract, useful for holographic duals and for writing tests.
papers.limitation: Theory survey / construction; no hardware demonstration.

papers.title: Observation of gravity-like signatures in holographic codes on a quantum computer
papers.coreIdea: The HaPPY holographic code, a hyperbolic tensor-network QEC, was run on trapped ions and showed gravity-like signatures in the code’s entanglement geometry.
papers.whyItMatters: Moves holographic encoding from analogy to a device-level experiment. Directly relevant to replacing the simulator’s block-average ‘encoder’.
papers.limitation: Toy code, small system. ‘Gravity-like’ is a diagnostic, not laboratory gravity.

papers.title: A fractional quantum Hall factory on quantum processors: constant-depth preparation of clustered non-Abelian states
papers.coreIdea: A surprising inversion: clustered non-Abelian FQH states can be prepared with system-size-independent two-qubit depth, while the Abelian Laughlin state needs linear depth.
papers.whyItMatters: If exotic is cheaper to prepare than ordinary, the DBE should prefer the computationally richer anyons for state-prep cost as well as for gates.
papers.limitation: Circuit constructions and numerics; not a Hall-bar experiment.

papers.title: Statistical mechanics and symmetries of non-Abelian anyon proliferation: from deformation to decoherence
papers.coreIdea: Whether a non-Abelian topological order survives messy preparation and decoherence is answered by a statistical-mechanics model whose symmetries track the corrupting anyons. Applied to D₄.
papers.whyItMatters: DBE cannot assume a perfect topological phase. This is the right language for ‘how much noise kills the braid core’.
papers.limitation: Worked example is D₄, which is not fusion-universal. S₃ stability still needs the same treatment.

papers.title: Integer linear programming decoder for Abelian and non-Abelian topological codes
papers.coreIdea: Matching decoders fail once fusion rules mix anyon species. An ILP decoder uses the actual fusion data and handles correlated noise for both Abelian and non-Abelian codes.
papers.whyItMatters: S₃ fusion space is exactly the setting where pair-matching is the wrong algorithm. This is a candidate decoder for the DBE core.
papers.limitation: ILP scaling vs real-time plasma control is the open engineering question.

papers.title: Protected logical qudits in Kitaev quantum double models via stable representations
papers.coreIdea: A representation-theoretic way to carve protected logical qudits out of quantum doubles — the same family as S₃.
papers.whyItMatters: The 2026 experiment encodes a qutrit in C₂ fluxes. This paper is the algebraic hygiene for that encoding.
papers.limitation: Algebraic; does not replace the bureau-of-standards relative encoding against local leakage.

papers.title: Trapping e/4 quasiparticles in bilayer graphene
papers.coreIdea: Quarter-charged quasiparticles — the FQH objects that can host non-Abelian statistics — are trapped in bilayer graphene, a materials platform rather than a gate-model simulation.
papers.whyItMatters: A reminder that anyons also live in real Hall fluids, not only in quantum processors. Parallel hardware path for the braid core.
papers.limitation: Trapping a charge-e/4 object is not yet braiding it. Interferometry remains the hard step.

papers.title: Experimental demonstration of the advantage of adaptive quantum circuits
papers.coreIdea: Adaptive circuits (measure, then choose the next gate) outperform purely unitary ones on hardware for preparing certain entangled resources.
papers.whyItMatters: Adaptive depth is the scalability story for quantum doubles. This is the experimental culture those protocols assume.
papers.limitation: Advantage is shown for specific tasks, not for a full topological compiler.

papers.title: Integrated AI plasma control on DIII-D
papers.coreIdea: A 2026 Nuclear Fusion paper describing an integrated AI control system on DIII-D — diagnostics in, coil/gyrotron commands out — the published attach surface for Bus A.
papers.whyItMatters: Modular interface exists. This is how DBE attaches to a machine that is already running, without owning the tokamak.
papers.limitation: Does not put a quantum processor in the loop, and should not: tearing growth times vs job-queue latency is a kill test.

papers.title: Nature Communications 16, 61493 (2025)
papers.coreIdea: A 2025 Nature Communications paper in the program library on quantum / topological matter, retained as a lookback pillar-adjacent source.
papers.whyItMatters: Year-back corpus: the observatory’s first runs are not allowed to be only this week’s arXiv.
papers.limitation: Secondary to the S₃ / RL / holography flagships for DBE scoring.

papers.title: Proof of a positive coherent-error threshold for topological quantum codes
papers.coreIdea: Real gates often make coherent over-rotations, not random bit flips. This paper proves that quantum LDPC codes with a bounded number of logicals — including the surface code — still have a positive threshold against coherent Z rotations.
papers.whyItMatters: DBE braids will be miscalibrated, not just Poisson-noisy. A theorem for coherent errors is more honest than a stochastic threshold.
papers.limitation: Proof is for coherent Z-type rotations and ML Pauli recovery; generic non-Pauli coherent noise and non-Abelian decoders are not covered.

papers.title: Scalable simulation of quantum dynamics on topological quantum hardware
papers.coreIdea: Compile molecular and condensed-phase time evolution onto Fibonacci and Ising anyons using Solovay–Kitaev, from two-level systems up through spin-boson models and reaction kinetics.
papers.whyItMatters: This is a proposed new pillar: the topological core should simulate dynamics, not only store a stability bit. That is how a braid engine becomes a plasma predictor.
papers.limitation: Compilation study, not a running topological processor. Resource counts vs tokamak real-time remain open, and chaos/I/O no-gos still apply.

papers.title: Non-Abelian anyon condensation: a path-integral Monte Carlo approach
papers.coreIdea: A sign-free Monte Carlo method for condensing anyons in Kitaev quantum doubles. For S₃, proliferating a non-Abelian electric anyon drives a first-order transition in which all nontrivial electric anyons condense.
papers.whyItMatters: S₃ is the 2026 hardware anyon theory. Condensation/confinement diagrams tell you which noise processes destroy the phase the DBE wants to sit in.
papers.limitation: Equilibrium path-integral, not a driven reactor environment. First-order transitions can be unforgiving in a device.

papers.title: A modular, topology-aware software stack for entanglement-based distributed quantum computing
papers.coreIdea: An open-source compiler/scheduler that partitions circuits across a network of QPUs, respecting both chip connectivity and entanglement-link topology.
papers.whyItMatters: DBE is modular by design (braid core, memory, clock, encoder, actuators). A topology-aware stack is the software analogue of that hardware split.
papers.limitation: Entanglement-based DQC, not anyon braiding, and not fusion-plant I/O. Treat as architecture, not plasma control.

papers.title: Statistical delocalization in the anyonic Aubry–André model
papers.coreIdea: Exchange statistics alone can push an anyonic chain toward delocalisation, even without density-density interactions — the opposite of the usual many-body localisation story.
papers.whyItMatters: A reminder that anyon statistics is a dynamical resource, not only a gate-set label. Could matter for how information spreads in a noisy braid core.
papers.limitation: 1D quasiperiodic model. Far from 2D topological order or a reactor.

papers.title: Floquet Majorana XYZ codes with tunable logical dynamics
papers.coreIdea: A Floquet code built from the Majorana XYZ subsystem code. Depending on lattice parity and the measurement schedule, a logical qubit can be static or forced to walk with the cycle — the same degree of freedom in two dynamical costumes.
papers.whyItMatters: Suggested new pillar: the clock and the Majorana register can be one object. That collapses two DBE subsystems into a single Floquet-Majorana layer.
papers.limitation: Lattice construction. Local Majorana parity measurements at scale are still hardware-hard.

papers.title: End-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics with bounded quantum advantage
papers.coreIdea: A sober resource analysis of quantum algorithms for nonlinear fluids: where a speedup can exist, and which I/O and chaos bottlenecks eat it.
papers.whyItMatters: DBE-S and the plasma controller will be tempted to claim quantum CFD. This paper is the adult supervision: bounded advantage, explicit bottlenecks — exactly the ‘don’t overclaim’ discipline the program asked for.
papers.limitation: Does not model a tokamak, and a bounded speedup is not a Q = 1000 plan.

papers.title: Fractional vortices in a spin-isotropic spiral spin liquid
papers.coreIdea: Classical spiral spin liquids host half-vortices whose fusion rules look like Ising anyons — fractional 2π windings in spin and momentum space.
papers.whyItMatters: A condensed-matter appearance of Ising-like fusion outside the usual Kitaev/FQH settings. Materials intuition for the braid core.
papers.limitation: Classical topological defects, not demonstrated non-Abelian quantum computation.

papers.title: Why Cooper pairs live in AdS₂: a spectral analysis of the Yukawa-SYK model
papers.coreIdea: A spectral look at why pairing in a Yukawa-SYK model organises itself as an AdS₂ problem — holography showing up inside a condensed-matter Hamiltonian.
papers.whyItMatters: Keeps the holography pillar connected to pairing/superconductivity, not only to toy QEC codes.
papers.limitation: Not a plasma compressor and not a fault-tolerant encoder.

papers.title: Error-adaptive quasi-local decoding of the toric code
papers.coreIdea: Global decoders are accurate but slow; strictly local rules are fast but miss long-range error structure. This paper makes that tradeoff operational for the dephased toric code with a quasi-local, error-adaptive decoder.
papers.whyItMatters: A DBE braid core sitting next to a tokamak cannot wait on a globally optimal matching. Decoder latency is part of the control budget.
papers.limitation: Abelian toric code, not S₃ / non-Abelian fusion decoding. Quasi-local is still not a real-time plasma-control proof.

papers.title: Landscape geometry of Majorana zero modes in inhomogeneous superconductors
papers.coreIdea: When a superconductor is messy — not a perfect crystal — the usual band-topology labels stop answering the only engineering question that matters: does a Majorana zero mode still sit at this defect? The paper recasts that as a geometric landscape problem.
papers.whyItMatters: DBE treats Majorana as a watch item, not a load-bearing qubit. A geometry that can fail in inhomogeneous devices is exactly the distinguisher the freeze demanded.
papers.limitation: Theory on inhomogeneous models, not an independent X and Z logical qubit. Cannot raise E-MZM above C1.

papers.title: Non-Abelian chiral spin liquid in a spin-1 antiferromagnet on the square lattice
papers.coreIdea: A short-range spin-1 magnet on the square lattice is argued to host a non-Abelian chiral spin liquid — the condensed-matter cousin of Fibonacci/Ising anyons — without needing a fractional quantum Hall fluid.
papers.whyItMatters: Keeps the anyon library honest: S3 on a processor is the hardware primitive we have; lattice spin liquids are a parallel materials path, not a replacement.
papers.limitation: Numerical / model evidence. Not a gate set, not a reactor part, and not S3.

papers.title: Shot noise signatures of Majorana-assisted transport in an Aharonov-Bohm interferometer
papers.coreIdea: Shot noise and the Fano factor in a two-dot Aharonov-Bohm loop coupled to topological wires are proposed as a transport fingerprint of Majorana-assisted tunneling.
papers.whyItMatters: The freeze requires a distinguisher for trivial Andreev / YSR mimics. Noise interferometry is one proposed test, not a completed one.
papers.limitation: Transport signatures remain mimic-prone. No public X+Z logical. Caps E-MZM at C1.

papers.title: Fractalizing spacetime: Floquet codes with fractonic excitations that are immobile in space and time
papers.coreIdea: A Floquet (periodically measured) code whose excitations cannot move in space or in time — a spacetime fracton. Memory and clock become the same object on paper.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the cleanest 2026 argument for unifying two HOLD items (fracton memory and time-crystal clock). The protocol still forbids making either load-bearing hardware.
papers.limitation: Circuit theory. Does not beat the D1 / cut-as-hardware rule. Queued as a new-pillar candidate, not auto-promoted.

papers.title: The Fusion Equilibrium Challenge: inferring magnetic geometry without magnetic diagnostics
papers.coreIdea: A challenge problem: reconstruct tokamak magnetic geometry when the usual magnetic probes are missing or untrusted — the exact I/O shape a modular controller must survive.
papers.whyItMatters: Bus A is 'diagnostics in, actuators out.' A published equilibrium-inference challenge is a bake-off surface for the control container.
papers.limitation: Challenge paper, not a DIII-D shot that beat the lab baseline. Does not by itself pass M2.

papers.title: Real-time virtual circuits for plasma shape control via neural network emulators: experimental demonstration
papers.coreIdea: Neural emulators stand in for slow magnetic diagnostics so a shape controller can close the loop in real time. Demonstrated as virtual circuits, not as a new coil.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the attach language of Bus A: latency-bounded commands, safe-hold on packet loss, no quantum hardware required.
papers.limitation: Preprint. Auto-Gate A5 blocks a C raise from bare arXiv. Strengthens the attach story, not the C score.

papers.title: Reconstructing non-Abelian braiding and fusion without anyon transport
papers.coreIdea: You do not have to drag anyons across a chip to know their braid and fusion data. Measurement-based reconstruction can recover the same topological matrices.
papers.whyItMatters: S3 on H2 already used linear-depth motion plus fusion. A transport-free reconstruction is how those primitives become constant-depth adaptive circuits — the scalable story in the Nature 2026 paper.
papers.limitation: Theory / numerics, not a second hardware replica of Lo et al. INCLUDE under E-S3; no C move.

papers.title: Runaway electron control by self-excited waves
papers.coreIdea: Runaway electrons — the beam that can punch a hole in a tokamak wall after a disruption — can be scattered by waves the plasma itself grows, not only by an external antenna.
papers.whyItMatters: Bus A’s fail-safe is disruption handling. A self-excited-wave actuator is a candidate command channel next to coils and pellets.
papers.limitation: Not RL, not a published DIII-D API win. INCLUDE only.

papers.title: Holographic quantum codes with trapped ions
papers.coreIdea: A proposal to embed holographic quantum error-correcting codes in a trapped-ion register — the same hardware class as the S3 experiment, used here for AdS/CFT-style codes rather than quantum doubles.
papers.whyItMatters: Shows holography remains a reading-list QEC idea on hardware we actually have. The freeze still cuts it as a reactor/processor subsystem.
papers.limitation: On the denylist for INCLUDE into the engine. Catalog as library only; no CUT reversal.

papers.title: Laser-assisted deuterium–tritium fusion in strong fields
papers.coreIdea: A Floquet / Volkov calculation of DT tunneling in a laser field. Significant enhancement at 1 keV ion energy appears only for electric fields around 10^15–10^16 V/m and photon energies ≲ 1 keV — XFEL territory, not a tokamak RF antenna.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the strongest published bound on DBE-S Layer 2. It does not kill the mechanism. It kills cheap versions of it.
papers.limitation: Nuclear theory, not a gain shot. Competing schemes (Crank–Nicolson vs Volkov) still disagree at the edges. Required field is the fail threshold for M4.

papers.title: High-intensity laser enhancement of DT fusion: 7–70% at extreme irradiance
papers.coreIdea: A second strong-field calculation finds only 7–70% DT-rate enhancement, and only at irradiances of 10^27–10^29 W/cm^2.
papers.whyItMatters: Together with PRC 109 this is the Layer-2 kill envelope: if after hole-burning and SRS/SBS the required I still exceeds reachable XFEL by >10×, Layer 2 leaves the plant path.
papers.limitation: Does not include spectral hole burning or parametric scatter. Those corrections go in the conservative direction.

papers.title: Dynamically assisted nuclear fusion
papers.coreIdea: A time-dependent electromagnetic kick can raise the tunneling probability through a Coulomb barrier — dynamically assisted fusion — without heating the whole Maxwell tail.
papers.whyItMatters: Ancestor of DBE-S Layer 2. Establishes the math (C2) while leaving the plant path at C1 until fields are reachable.
papers.limitation: Does not put Q = 1000 on a machine. Drive energy is an auxiliary term the ledger must count.

papers.title: Dynamically assisted tunneling in the Floquet picture
papers.coreIdea: Tunneling through a time-periodic barrier is rewritten in Floquet language so multiphoton channels are explicit instead of being faked by a static WKB shift.
papers.whyItMatters: The DBE-S revision’s first complaint was naive WKB. This is the textbook correction those notebooks omitted.
papers.limitation: Single-particle theory. Plasma Lindblad, hole burning, and radiation are not in the Hamiltonian.

papers.title: Avoiding fusion plasma tearing instability with deep reinforcement learning
papers.coreIdea: A deep-RL agent on DIII-D predicted tearing-mode onset and adjusted plasma shape/beta in time to avoid the instability, using the real coil set.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the first attach point of DBE. Bus A already talks to a real plant in this paper’s language.
papers.limitation: Avoiding tearing is not Q = 1000, and the agent is classical. Quantum hardware is not in this loop — and should not be, per the latency kill test.

papers.title: AI surrogate modeling for real-time tokamak equilibrium prediction
papers.coreIdea: Neural surrogates of Grad–Shafranov equilibria are benchmarked for real-time use: milliseconds instead of a full reconstructive solve.
papers.whyItMatters: Bus A’s latency budget lives or dies on how fast the observer is. A published surrogate bake-off is a metric, not a slogan.
papers.limitation: Offline/near-online. Chaos and tearing growth times still bound any in-loop quantum processor.

papers.title: Assessing the effect of error field penetration during plasma current ramp-up in the DIII-D tokamak
papers.coreIdea: On DIII-D, n=1 error-field thresholds measured in flattop still apply during Ip ramp-up. Above 2–3 kA of 3D coil current, MHD modes get seeded.
papers.whyItMatters: C4 on the relevant machine. Coil-current numbers and ramp-up windows are the kind of actuator bound Bus A can attach to.
papers.limitation: Classical MHD/error-field study. No quantum hardware, and it does not by itself close a tearing-avoidance RL loop.

papers.title: Discrete time crystals in disordered anisotropic Heisenberg chains
papers.coreIdea: Matrix-product simulations find discrete time-crystalline order in disordered Heisenberg spin chains, including the isotropic point, under periodic drive.
papers.whyItMatters: Keeps the many-body physics of Floquet time crystals current. That is allowed as a study. It is not allowed as the system metronome.
papers.limitation: Numerics on 1D chains. Prethermal lifetime vs a control horizon is still the kill test, and it is not passed here.

papers.title: Phase-Controlled Majorana Zero Modes in Altermagnetic Topological-Insulator Josephson Junctions
papers.coreIdea: Altermagnetic order in a topological-insulator Josephson junction lets a phase bias park and move Majorana modes via facet-dependent Andreev shifts.
papers.whyItMatters: Another proposed MZM knob. Logged under WATCH. Novelty of materials is Adoption, not Confidence.
papers.limitation: Proposal / model. No public logical qubit.

papers.title: kobra: a new Vlasov code intended for plasma-wall modeling
papers.coreIdea: A finite-volume Vlasov solver for sheath-scale plasma–wall physics. Unlike PIC, it evolves the full distribution function and so does not undersample velocity space.
papers.whyItMatters: S-L3 says keep the solvers and do not skip hole-burning / SRS-SBS. A public Vlasov code is exactly the Bus C tool the ledger is allowed to use.
papers.limitation: Sheath / wall code, not a driven-Coulomb-barrier fusion-rate engine. Does not move Layer 2 off HOLD.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Particle Dynamics in Fusion Plasmas: Orbital Tomography and Spectrum Analysis for Energy and Momentum Transport under Resonant Non-Axisymmetric Perturbations
papers.coreIdea: A thesis-scale study of how resonant magnetic perturbations move particles of different energies, with a cheap orbital-tomography diagnostic for transport.
papers.whyItMatters: RMP coils are a DBE actuator. Knowing which velocity classes they empty is the classical cousin of spectral hole-burning.
papers.limitation: Thesis, not a plant Q. No Floquet nuclear tunneling.

papers.title: ELMO: An Uncertainty-Aware Simulation-to-Surrogate Workflow for Fast Pedestal Linear-Stability Prediction
papers.coreIdea: BOUT++ pedestal stability is too slow for operating-space search. ELMO trains an uncertainty-aware surrogate so linear ELM/peeling-ballooning predictions come back fast enough to be useful.
papers.whyItMatters: Bus B’s job is offline and near-online optimization against a classical baseline. A pedestal surrogate is a bake-off target, not a quantum claim.
papers.limitation: Linear MHD surrogate. Fail if a quantum path is slower or less accurate on the same model.

papers.title: Deep learning emergent spacetime from fermionic spectral functions in holography
papers.coreIdea: A physics-informed neural ODE reconstructs the bulk metric of a charged AdS black hole from boundary fermionic spectral functions, with UV/horizon constraints baked into the net.
papers.whyItMatters: Interesting AdS/CFT inverse problem. It stays in the reading list. It does not sit on the bus.
papers.limitation: Holography as a reactor or processor subsystem is on the denylist (E-HOL CUT). One paper cannot un-cut it.

papers.title: Realization of decoherence-induced averaged symmetry-protected topological phases on quantum processors
papers.coreIdea: Open-system decoherence can create an averaged symmetry-protected topological phase that only exists after you average over trajectories. The team realised it on programmable processors.
papers.whyItMatters: Noise as a resource for topology, not only an error. Relevant to how a braid core looks once it is coupled to a hot plant. Library INCLUDE for E-QEC, C capped at 3 (wrong platform for a reactor).
papers.limitation: Processor analog. G5: does not treat a QPU demo as a tokamak result.

papers.title: Few-body bound states in the anyon-Hubbard model
papers.coreIdea: Fractional exchange statistics in the 1D anyon-Hubbard model bind few-body clusters that ordinary bosons or fermions would not form the same way.
papers.whyItMatters: Anyon statistics as a dynamical resource in cold atoms. Off the engine path but on-field for the library.
papers.limitation: 1D Hubbard physics, not 2D topological order.

papers.title: Topological superconductors and Majorana fermions based on X-wave magnets with X = p, d, f, g, i
papers.coreIdea: Altermagnets and odd-parity magnets coupled to s-wave superconductors produce a zoo of topological superconducting phases, some hosting Majorana modes, depending on magnetic strength and filling.
papers.whyItMatters: Materials catalog for the MZM WATCH file. Adoption of altermagnet papers does not raise Confidence.
papers.limitation: Phase-diagram theory. No logical qubit.

papers.title: NIF scientific gain Q_sci = 4.13 (8.6 MJ out / 2.08 MJ on target)
authors: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, National Ignition Facility
papers.coreIdea: The only public platform with scientific gain above one reached Q_sci = 4.13 in April 2025. That is fusion energy out over energy on target, not plant electricity.
papers.whyItMatters: Ground truth that constrains the moonshot. Q = 1000 is not on any public machine roadmap. The baseline got real; the slogan did not get easier.
papers.limitation: Q_sci is not Q_eng. Drive, pumping, and conversion are still on the plant side of the ledger.

papers.title: Real-time virtual circuits for plasma shape control via neural network emulators: integration and testing in the MAST-U PCS
papers.coreIdea: The companion engineering paper: how the neural virtual-circuit controller was wired into MAST Upgrade’s actual plasma control system and tested before the shot.
papers.whyItMatters: Interface contracts (in/out/latency/fail-safe) are what make a module a module. This is the PCS-integration evidence Bus A needs.
papers.limitation: Integration and testing write-up, not a Q-gain result.

papers.coreIdea: For full-rank density matrices the state space is contractible, the Uhlmann bundle is topologically trivial, and the holonomy admits no quantized invariants; although the Uhlmann phase is genuinely geometric, this topological poverty has kept it from serving as a robust physical .

papers.title: A Functorial Theory of Defects in Abelian Chern-Simons Theory
papers.coreIdea: Abelian Chern-Simons theories can be written as categorical TQFTs, so defects (domain walls, anyon lines) become first-class objects you can extend the theory with, not afterthoughts.
papers.whyItMatters: Defects are how lattice hardware actually hosts anyons. A functorial language for them is a cleaner compiler target than ad-hoc string operators.
papers.limitation: Abelian Chern-Simons is not the S3 non-Abelian order. This does not move E-S3 off C3.

papers.title: Shape Deformation and Braid Statistics of Fractional Quantum Hall Quasiparticles
papers.coreIdea: Fractional quantum Hall quasiparticles stay anyonic even when their shape deforms: the Berry phase of a braid is robust to the size and outline of the loop, not just to an idealized point particle.
papers.whyItMatters: Braiding on hardware is never a perfect worldline. Shape-robust braid statistics is the difference between a gate that survives a messy anyon and a phase that washes out.
papers.limitation: The result is for FQH 'ideal anyons' in a continuum model, not an S3 quantum-double circuit on trapped ions.
